title: Nursing
credential: Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

• UW Bothell general transfer admissions requirements: 
* English Proficiency as deemed required by the Office of Admissions 
• Associate degree in Nursing or diploma in nursing 
• Active unencumbered Registered Nurse licensure in the State of Washington 
Applicants pending passage of the NCLEX are conditionally admitted for two quarters.
• A minimum of 90 quarter credits 
• English Composition: 5 credits 
• Arts & Humanities: 10 credits 
• Statistics: 4 to 5 credits 
• Microbiology: 3 to 5 credits 
• Anatomy & Physiology with a Lab: 10 credits

*Chemistry: 5 credits
• A minimum grade of 2.0 or higher in all BSN prerequisite coursework outlined above
• National and State Criminal Background Check with acceptable results
sourceText.degree-completion:
Completion Requirements

Transfer Credit - 90
NCLEX-RN Exam Completion Credits - 45
Upper-Division Nursing Courses - 35
Upper Division Non-Nursing UWB Electives - 10
90 credits must be upper division (300-400 level)
Completion of last 45 credits at UWB
Cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher
Minimum 2.0 grade in all BSN degree program coursework

rules.sourceText:
Core Courses



The curriculum is based on the American Association of Colleges of Nursing Essentials of Baccalaureate Education for Professional Nursing Practice and the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education. Core courses are each 5 credits. To progress in the program, students must earn a minimum 2.0 GPA in each course.  View course descriptions in the UW Bothell catalog.






BNURS 360: Critical Reading and Information Literacy in Nursing



BNURS 420: Health Policy and the Organization of Healthcare



BNURS 421: Social Justice in Health



BNURS 422: Team Leadership and Care Coordination



BNURS 423: Ethical and Quality Nursing Care



BNURS 424: Population-Based Health in Community Practice



B NURS 460: Translating Scholarly Knowledge to Nursing Practice

Fieldwork Participation 



Before beginning the fieldwork course, Population-Based Health in Community Practice, students must complete and maintain required immunizations, health screenings, safety training, and professional requirements. Requirements include COVID-19, Hepatitis B, MMR, Varicella, TB, TDaP, and seasonal influenza immunizations and screenings; an active, unencumbered RN license; American Heart Association BLS/CPR certification; UW School of Nursing HIPAA training; an annual background check and criminal disclosure; and required policy acknowledgments and authorization forms completed through the program’s designated compliance system. Fees apply. These requirements were created with our community partners and may be stricter than individual healthcare employers.

bullets: The catalog describes conditional admission for two quarters for applicants awaiting NCLEX passage; verify current eligibility and timing.
This route continues prior nursing education. Transcript coursework alone does not establish licensure or clinical eligibility.
Camino does not award 45 NCLEX completion credits or create earned coursework when this program is selected.
The published seven-course core is 35 credits with a minimum 2.0 in each course. Fieldwork, electives, GPA and residency remain separate checks.
